items: New: KeyBelt checks for PyMEL (other tools need it) and offers a one-click install when it is missing; status and button in Settings > General > Maya Preferences.

Time Dragger HUD: on a fresh Maya the key is routed even when Maya's hotkeys load late (retries for a few seconds at startup); recognises any spelling of Maya's Time Dragger command; when it can't take over the key, or falls back to Maya's own Time Dragger, the Script Editor says why.
Public beta: the whole toolset is now labelled beta. The Settings window title, version label and Updates card show "beta".
Motion Trail is no longer flagged beta. It is built on the Agora Community motion trail, used as the base, then modified and improved for KeyBelt.
Motion Trail moved from Secondary motion to the Baking / curve tools group (yellow) in the timeline toolbar and the docs.
Settings > General > Updates: new Send feedback button, opens the feedback page in your browser with your KeyBelt and Maya versions filled in.

Automatic updates: KeyBelt downloads and verifies new versions in the background and installs them the next time Maya starts, with a short "Updated to x.y.z" message. On by default (Settings > General > Updates > Update KeyBelt automatically). By hand, one button goes Check for updates → Update to x.y.z → Restart Maya to finish.

Documentation restyled to match the KeyBelt website (dark / light theme, Inter font bundled for offline use, tool icons in the sidebar) and extended with a mission note and a Working with KeyBelt windows section (MMB drag to move, RMB drag to resize).

Documentation shows the real tool windows, lists every toolbar button with its icon (separate from the sliders), explains Offseter step by step (timeline range + blend frames, selected keys, whole curve) and has a new Viewport Bar page.

One-step install and automatic updates: drag drag_n_drop.py into Maya and KeyBelt installs itself to Documents/maya/KeyBelt (shared by every Maya version). Settings > General > Updates checks for new versions in the background; nothing is downloaded until you click Download update, and the update is applied the next time Maya starts. KeyBelt now ships as a compiled, protected build under a free-to-use license (EULA.txt).

Maya preference helpers: asset-centric selection and Maya's cycle check warnings are turned off at every launch (Settings > General > Maya Preferences, on by default). Unticking restores your previous Maya values.

Time Dragger HUD: hold the Time Dragger key and drag (LMB / MMB) for an endless scrub with a temporary timeline showing the range, keys of the selection and bookmarks. Shift = fine, Ctrl = coarse, wheel = one frame, Esc = cancel. Toggle in Settings > General > Time Dragger (off = Maya's own Time Dragger). Only a key still bound to Maya's Time Dragger is rerouted.

Settings window reorganised: General / Toolbars / Hotkeys / Radial & Viewport Bar / Documentation. Timeline Tools and Graph Editor are merged into Toolbars (one action-button list with timeline + Graph Editor columns); Quick Access is now Radial & Viewport Bar with one shared tool palette. General uses cards (Toolbar, Keys Sliders, Time Dragger, Startup, Session).
The Radial Menu tool palette no longer lists the Settings tool itself.
Graph Editor toolbar sliders now stretch to the free width (48–240 px each) and the toolbar never forces the Graph Editor to stay wide: when it's too narrow, it is cut off at the right edge.
Keys Editor: the action row no longer overlaps. Bake is now icon-only and uses the Baker icon. The row fits on one line at the default width and wraps when narrower.
Timeline toolbar: the Delete Flat button shows its icon instead of "DF".
New Selector icon.
Graph Editor toolbar sliders: middle-click opens the same effect popup as the timeline sliders, with an extra "Remove this slider" row.
Offseter: Undo / Redo no longer offsets the curve again; the restored values become the new baseline.
Viewport Bar stays visible while Maya is in the background.
Baker: the current time is always restored after Bake to Circle, even if the bake fails early.
Keys Editor effect table (names, short codes, colours) now has one source (KeysEditor/keys_effects.py) shared by the Keys Editor, timeline and viewport sliders.
Maya 2026 / PySide6 compatibility fixes (fontMetrics().width and QApplication.desktop() fallbacks, Viewport Bar timer slots, Keys Editor wave field crash on close).
Reset Translate / Rotate / Scale no longer need PyMEL (failed on Maya 2026); one undo step, locked channels skipped.
Settings → Timeline Tools: readable category headers on light colours, visible check boxes, letter icon for tools without one.

Namespaced as the package keybelt. KeyBelt used generic top-level module names (main, styles, RadialMenu, ViewportBar, ...) that clashed with other toolsets loaded in the same Maya session. The KeyBelt folder is no longer put on sys.path; it is registered explicitly as the package keybelt (independent of the folder name) and every internal import is keybelt.-qualified. The startup/shelf/hotkey/uiScript command strings embed the absolute folder and re-register the package when needed. The old "purge same-named modules from outside the KeyBelt folder" step is gone, and the unload scriptJob sweep only matches keybelt callbacks. Maya-global names that could collide (window object names, _tool_id, optionVar, menu and condition names) are now keybelt-prefixed.

Migration (one time): re-drop drag_n_drop.py (or toggle Settings > General > Startup > Load at Maya startup off and on) to regenerate the shelf button and the userSetup.py block. An old block that still does import keybelt_core keeps working through a compatibility forward, but it also purges same-named modules of other toolsets, so migrate it.

Added the Graph Editor toolbar (GraphEditorToolbar): KeysEditor effect sliders and action buttons attached to the Graph Editor panel, with a new Settings > Graph Editor tab (enable / disable, button order and visibility). Unload stops it too.

Added a "Load at Maya startup" checkbox (Settings > General > Startup) that adds / removes the KeyBelt block in the versioned userSetup.py (takes effect next launch; keybelt_core.is_startup_enabled() / set_startup_enabled()). The block logic now lives in keybelt_startup.py, shared with the installer; a userSetup.py.bak backup is written before each change.

Removed the KeyBelt tool-list window. Launching is now headless (timeline toolbar, viewport bar, radial menu hotkey); show_docked() / show_floating() are kept as aliases of show(), and a stale main-window workspace control restored from an old layout is removed automatically.
Added keybelt_core.unload_all() and an "Unload KeyBelt" button (Settings > General > Session) to unload KeyBelt from the running Maya session without restarting.

All tools now run on both PySide2 (Maya 2022-2024) and PySide6 (Maya 2025+) via the new keybelt_qt.py shim; removed PySide(1)/PyQt4 fallbacks and PySide6-removed APIs (fm.width, QDesktopWidget, globalPos/pos on events, exec_).
First public release of KeyBelt, an animation toolset for Maya.
Tools: Baker, Keys Editor, Offseter, Reset All, Selector, Motion Trail.
Dockable tool window, timeline toolbar with Keys Editor sliders, floating Viewport Bar, radial menu (default Alt+Q) and a Settings window (toolbars, hotkeys, quick access, docs).
Local HTML documentation (Settings > Documentation).
Drag and drop installer: KeyBelt shelf tab plus auto-start through userSetup.py; uninstall() helper.
